subject: Error message using modavg function (AICcmodavg package) - Parameter not found

messages.author: b7318121e2d91003
messages.subject: Error message using modavg function (AICcmodavg package) - Parameter not found
parts:
Good afternoon,

Just wondering if anyone has experienced the following error when using the modavg function (AICcmodavg package). I am using PCount models for lake trout distribution and trying to average the estimate of mean depth ("MeanD") for my top models. I am able to find the average for a slope parameter but not mean depth or mean depth squared ("MeanD2") and for another fish species I am able to find the MeanD average and MeanD2 average so I am not sure why it wont work in this scenario.  

"Error in modavg.AICunmarkedFitPCount(LTcand.set, parm = "MeanD", modnames = NULL,  : 
  
Parameter not found in any of the candidate models"

The code that received the error: 

LTMeanDavg = modavg(LTcand.set, parm = "MeanD", modnames =
                    NULL, second.ord = TRUE, nobs = NULL, uncond.se = "revised",
                  conf.level = 0.95, exclude = list("MeanD2"), warn = TRUE, c.hat = 1,
                  parm.type = "lambda") 

Thanks,
Ty

messages.author: 4e956cc50ac3e075
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Error message using modavg function (AICcmodavg package) - Parameter not found
parts:
Ty,


If the code works for one species, but not the other, it might be that some models cannot estimate the parameter you are interested in. Are the model lists for both species identical? A first place to start would be to do a quick check with the function extractX(your.model.list) to see if the output is identical. Also, you might want to consider model-averaging with shrinkage instead (modavgShrink( )), especially if you have a lot of uncertainty regarding the top models, or looking at the model-averaged predictions (modavgPred( )) as a function of different values of your explanatory variable.


Best,


Marc

messages.author: 4e956cc50ac3e075
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Error message using modavg function (AICcmodavg package) - Parameter not found
parts:
Hi Ty,

The difference between both is that modavg( ) computes the "natural
average" of the estimate (Burnham and Anderson 2002, p. 152). If you
have several models that share the support, then this estimate could be
biased high (Cade 2015: Ecology 96, 2370--2382), because it only
focuses on the models that include the parameter of interest. In such a
case, model-averaging with the shrinkage estimator is preferred
(Burnham and Anderson 2002, p. 152) as it includes all models (e.g.,
modavgShrink( )).

Regarding your issues with the two species, you can send me offlist
your code and data so I can take a look.

Hope it helps,

Marc
